is_anopheles.evidence: The study was conducted on wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. (consisting of An. coluzzii and An. gambiae s.s.) in experimental huts in Cove, Benin (page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No resistance markers were genotyped in this study. The mention of 'kdr (L1014F) allele frequency of 89%' on page 3 cites previous characterization of the Cove field site (Ngufor et al. 2015, ref [13]).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No de novo genotype data, counts, or sample sizes for marker testing are reported in the study.

african_field_population.evidence: Wild free-flying Anopheles gambiae s.l. entering experimental huts and larvae collected from rice paddies in Cove, Benin were tested (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary experimental hut trial evaluating chlorfenapyr and alpha-cypermethrin IRS.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study took place in Cove, Southern Benin (7°14'N, 2°18'E) (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collections and experimental hut trials were conducted between June and September 2015 (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard experimental hut trial performed at the LSHTM/CREC collaborative station in Cove, Benin.

supplement.evidence: The supplementary file S1 Table contains hut collection raw counts; no genotyping data was generated.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of indoor residual spraying (IRS) with chlorfenapyr alone or mixed with alpha-cypermethrin against wild Anopheles gambiae s.l. in experimental huts in Cove, Benin. Although bioassays and hut performance metrics were assessed, no molecular genotyping of insecticide resistance markers was conducted.
